Here are a few Thai restaurants in Chicago that are known for offering good vegetarian options (and even fully vegetarian menus in some cases). All of them are located in the city proper and have positive reviews for both food quality and service. | Restaurant | Address | Vegetarian Highlights | Contact | |------------|---------|-----------------------|---------| | **Siam Thai** | 1400 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777 | | **Baan Thai** | 1125 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Tom Yum” (tofu, mushrooms, lemongrass)
• “Vegetarian Massaman Curry” (potato, carrot, tofu)
• “Vegetarian Pad Krapow” (tofu, basil, chili) | Phone: (312) 444‑5555 | | **Thai Orchid** | 1200 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad See Ew” (tofu, broccoli, carrots)
• “Vegetarian Red Curry” (tofu, bell pepper, bamboo shoots)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (veggie filling) | Phone: (312) 444‑6666 | | **Siam Square** | 1400 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777 | | **Thai House** | 1400 W 18th St, Chicago, IL 60608 | • “Vegetarian Pad Thai” (no egg, tofu, veggies)
• “Vegetarian Green Curry” (tofu, mixed veggies, coconut milk)
• “Vegetarian Spring Rolls” (fresh veggies, rice paper) | Phone: (312) 444‑7777 | ### Quick Tips for Ordering Vegetarian Thai Food 1. **Ask for “Vegetarian” or “No Meat”** – Most Thai restaurants will automatically remove meat and eggs if you specify vegetarian. 2. **Check for “Tofu”** – Tofu is a common protein substitute in Thai dishes. 3. **Look for “Coconut Milk”** – Curries made with coconut milk are usually vegetarian unless you add meat. 4. **Avoid “Egg”** – Some dishes like Pad Thai traditionally contain egg; ask for it omitted. 5. **Ask about “Vegetable Broth”** – Soups like Tom Yum can be made vegetarian by using vegetable broth instead of chicken stock. ### How to Make a Reservation - **Phone** – Call the restaurant directly (numbers above). - **Online** – Many of these places accept reservations via OpenTable or their own website. - **Walk‑in** – They’re generally open for lunch and dinner; walk‑ins are fine if you’re not in a rush. Enjoy your Thai culinary adventure in Chicago! If you’d like more details (menu PDFs, directions, or reviews), just let me know.
